s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent chest pain and electrocardiographic changes
salient_findings: Paroxysmal chest pain occurring 5 times during the day
ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR on initial ECG
key_facts: Patient presented to the emergency department with chest pain
Chest pain was paroxysmal and occurred 5 times during the day
Each episode of chest pain lasted 15 to 30 minutes
Blood pressure was 106/52 mm Hg
Pulse rate was 64 beats per minute
Chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds with no murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolyte levels, kidney and liver function tests, B-type natriuretic peptide and D-dimer levels were all within normal limits
Cardiac troponin I level was elevated at 25 ng/mL
Initial ECG revealed sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
Repeated ECG showed sinus bradycardia, Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
Coronary angiography showed total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and total occlusion of the right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Unstable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent chest pain and electrocardiographic changes with subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery

shortlist.label: Variant angina
shortlist.why_kept: ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, suggestive of coronary artery spasm

shortlist.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Total occlusion of the right coronary artery and recurrent chest pain

shortlist.label: Coronary artery spasm
shortlist.why_kept: ST-segment elevation and recurrent chest pain, potentially indicative of vasospastic angina

raw.rationale: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and ECG changes including ST-segment elevation and Q wave in lead III, along with total occlusion of the right coronary artery on coronary angiography, are indicative of acute myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: Unstable angina typically does not present with elevated troponin levels or significant ECG changes like Q waves and ST-segment elevation.

rejected.label: Variant angina
rejected.why: Variant angina is characterized by chest pain at rest with transient ST-segment elevation, but it does not typically cause elevated troponin levels or Q waves on ECG.

rejected.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: While possible, the information provided does not specifically suggest dissection, and the findings are more consistent with acute myocardial infarction due to occlusion.

rejected.label: Coronary artery spasm
rejected.why: Coronary artery spasm could cause chest pain and some ECG changes, but the presence of elevated troponin, Q waves, and total occlusion of a coronary artery points more towards an acute myocardial infarction.
